title: Change the order to create the missing derivative
measure: L^2 on the plane; L^1 on each coordinate
hypotheses: D={0<x<y<1}; F=1_D exp(y^2) is Borel and 0<=F<=e 1_(0,1)^2.
result: Integral over D of exp(y^2) equals (e-1)/2.

title: A measurable region whose entire boundary has positive area
hypotheses: At stage n remove 2^(n-1) middle intervals of length 4^(-n); C is the remaining closed intersection; E=C x [0,1].
result: L^1(C)=1/2; boundary(E)=E; L^2(boundary(E))=1/2; integral_E 2y=1/2; the zero extension is not Riemann integrable.

title: A null measurable set with one nonmeasurable section
measure: Complete L^2 jointly; complete L^1 on sections
hypotheses: V subset [0,1] is non-Lebesgue measurable; E={0} x V. General proof assumes A is Lebesgue measurable in R^(m+n).
result: E is planar measurable and null, but E_0=V is nonmeasurable; arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable sets have measurable sections almost everywhere.

title: Two finite iterated integrals, but no signed Lebesgue integral
measure: L^2 on (0,1)^2; L^1 on each coordinate
hypotheses: f(x,y)=(x^2-y^2)/(x^2+y^2)^2 on (0,1)^2; every one-variable section is continuous and integrable.
result: Integrating y first gives pi/4; integrating x first gives -pi/4; both joint sign parts have infinite integral, so the signed Lebesgue integral is undefined.
